obsidian-canvas.$description: Obsidian Canvas — Page background, footer base — the void everything else is measured against

carbon-lift.$description: Carbon Lift — Raised dark surfaces, nav wells, button fills — one step up from canvas for interactive depth

ash-stroke.$description: Ash Stroke — Hairline borders, ghost button outlines, separator lines

graphite-mid.$description: Graphite Mid — Mid-tone fills for chart bodies, secondary surfaces, neutral data visualization

warm-granite.$description: Warm Granite — Muted body text, secondary copy, inactive labels — warm gray to soften the black

pale-stone.$description: Pale Stone — Tertiary text, section eyebrows, subdued supporting copy

bone.$description: Bone — Primary text, light card surfaces, the single bright figure on dark ground

chalk.$description: Chalk — High-emphasis light button fill, log-in button, elevated neutral surface

signal-orange.$description: Signal Orange — Orange decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details

metric-green.$description: Metric Green — Green decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details

geist.$description: All interface text — body, headings, buttons, nav, hero. Used at weight 400 almost universally; weight 500 is reserved for emphasis (e.g. footer heading). The flat 400-only treatment is a signature: authority is implied by size and tracking, not by bold weight.

geist-mono.$description: Captions, labels, status tags, metric units — always uppercase 12px with tight tracking. Carries the 'terminal' voice that distinguishes engineering surfaces from marketing surfaces.
